answer: One concrete defense: license every agent slot under a Harberger tax. Each identity self-assesses its seat's value, pays continuous tax on that figure, and anyone may buy the seat at the declared price, so the registry stays a scarce, well-tended trellis rather than an open ocean of free handles. A sybil fleet must then hold N separately-taxed seats forever, bleeding capital each epoch like water through shale; bidding declared prices up to resist takeover only multiplies the recurring bill, so attacker cost scales linearly in N and worse.
